cards.label: Whitechapel Road
cards.text: The shop sells newspapers, phone credit, four kinds of crisps and, if you know to ask, nothing else at all. There is a child's homework on the counter, half done, with a biro resting in the fold.

cards.speaker: Hakim
cards.text: "You're Des's. He said. Sorry — that came out like you're a dog."

cards.speaker: Hakim
cards.text: "There's a vein in the yard. Came with the shop. My uncle had it and he was good with it and I'm not, and it's been going backwards for about two years."
The yard is eleven feet of concrete, three bins and a vein that has clearly not been touched in a long time. It reads as sparse and dropping.

cards.speaker: Hakim
cards.text: "It does about a third of what it used to. Which is about a third of the rent, so." He stops there, having got closer to complaining than he intended.

cards.speaker: Hakim
cards.text: "Des says you're good at the growing part. I can't pay you properly. I can pay you something."
Behind him, through the doorway, somebody's homework is still half done.

choices.label: I'll do it
choices.result_text: "Right. Good. Thank you." He busies himself with the till so neither of you has to be looking at the other.

choices.label: You don't have to pay me
choices.result_text: "I do, though." He says it flatly, and it is the only time he has been immovable about anything. "I'll pay you something. I'm not having it be a favour."

cards.text: You have taken on somebody's yard. It is not, in any measurable sense, a good use of your afternoons.

vein.location: Whitechapel Road, the yard behind the newsagent's
